The Soviet Union decided almost everything in the alliance.
In 1968 troops of the Pact invaded Czechoslovakia and ended the Prague Spring.
The Warsaw Pact was dissolved on 1 July 1991.

abschnitte.text: Its official name was the “Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance”. The members promised to help each other militarily in the event of an attack. The supreme command was in Moscow and was always led by a Soviet officer. In this way the **Soviet Union** could control the armies of the other states.

After the Second World War Europe was divided by the **Iron Curtain**. In the West the USA and its allies joined together in **NATO** in 1949. When the Federal Republic of Germany joined NATO in May 1955, the Soviet Union founded the Warsaw Pact shortly afterwards. The two alliances faced each other heavily armed but never fought each other directly.

Its troops were used several times against people in its own member states. In 1956 Soviet troops crushed the **Hungarian Uprising**. In 1968 troops of the Soviet Union and other Pact states invaded Czechoslovakia to end the **Prague Spring**, a movement for more freedom. Albania withdrew from the alliance after that, and Romania had not taken part in the invasion.

In the late 1980s the Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev allowed more freedom. In 1989 the Berlin Wall fell and Communist rule ended in many countries of Eastern Europe. East Germany left in 1990 with German reunification. On 1 July 1991 the Warsaw Pact was officially dissolved, and at the end of 1991 the Soviet Union also broke up.

Many former members are now in NATO, for example Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary since 1999. Switzerland also felt the effects of the Pact: after 1956 it took in around 14,000 **refugees** from Hungary, and after 1968 around 12,000 from Czechoslovakia. Neutral Switzerland belonged to neither alliance. During the Cold War, however, its army prepared above all for a possible attack from the East.

begriffe.erklaerung: States promise to defend each other if one of them is attacked.
Tensions between East and West from about 1947 to 1991, without direct war between the great powers.
The heavily guarded border between Eastern and Western Europe.
An attempt in Czechoslovakia in 1968 to create more freedom.

gewusst: The Warsaw Pact never waged war against a country outside the alliance; its troops only invaded member states.
After 1968 Albania remained a formal member for a few more weeks and only officially left in September 1968.

teile.einleitung: The Special Drawing Right, SDR for short, is a special reserve asset of the International Monetary Fund (IMF). It is not money you can pay with in a shop. But countries can exchange it for real currencies.
wichtigste: The SDR is an international reserve asset that can be exchanged for currencies.
The IMF created Special Drawing Rights in 1969.
The currency basket consists of five currencies (as of 2025).
In 2016 the Chinese renminbi was added to the basket.
The US dollar has the greatest weight.
The ISO currency code is XDR.

abschnitte.text: A **Special Drawing Right** is not a real currency. It is a **claim** on the freely usable currencies of the members of the **International Monetary Fund** (IMF). A country can exchange its SDRs with other countries for dollars, euros or other currencies. In this way the SDR **supplements** countries' **currency reserves**. Currency reserves are money that a state keeps ready for emergencies. Switzerland has also been a member of the IMF since 1992.

The IMF created the SDR in **1969**. At that time **gold** and **dollars** were not enough as reserves, because world trade was growing strongly. The first allocation took place in **1970**. The SDR's code is **XDR**. Codes beginning with X stand for units without a country of their own, such as XAU for gold.

The value of the SDR is based on a **basket of currencies**. It consists of five currencies: the **US dollar**, the **euro**, the Chinese **renminbi**, the Japanese **yen** and the British **pound**. The Swiss franc is not included. The renminbi has been part of it since 1 October **2016**. At the 2022 review, the dollar was given a weight of about 43 per cent and the euro about 29 per cent. The weights are reset about every five years.

In a general allocation, each country receives SDRs in proportion to its **quota** at the IMF. The quota depends mainly on economic strength. That is why rich countries receive the most, which is often criticised. The largest allocation so far was in **August 2021**: about **456 billion SDRs**, worth about 650 billion dollars. It was meant to help deal with the consequences of the **Covid pandemic**.

gewusst: The Swiss franc is not part of the SDR currency basket.
The X at the start of XDR shows that this unit does not belong to any country.

teile.einleitung: The Food and Agriculture Organization, FAO for short, is the United Nations organisation for food and farming. It works to make sure that people around the world have enough to eat. It is based in Rome, and its founding day, 16 October, is now World Food Day.
wichtigste: The FAO is the UN organisation that works to make sure people around the world have enough to eat.
FAO stands for “Food and Agriculture Organization”.
It was founded on 16 October 1945 in Quebec, Canada.
Its headquarters have been in Rome since 1951.
Its Latin motto is “Fiat panis”, which means “Let there be bread”.
16 October is World Food Day every year.
The FAO supports farmers, fishers and foresters in poor countries.

abschnitte.text: The **FAO** is a specialised agency of the United Nations and one of the oldest parts of the UN family. Almost all the states of the world are members, as well as the European Union. Its aim is a world without **hunger**, in which everyone has healthy food. This aim is also set down as Goal 2 in the UN's Sustainable Development Goals.

The FAO advises countries on how to grow more and better food without destroying the soil. In emergencies it hands out seeds and tools to farmers. It fights animal diseases and plant pests, such as desert locusts, which can eat whole harvests. It also collects data worldwide on farming, **fishing** and forests.

Although enough food is produced on Earth for everyone, many people go hungry. According to the FAO, around 670 million people did in 2024. The main causes are poverty, wars, extreme weather caused by climate change and high food prices. At the same time about a third of all food is wasted or lost along the way; this is called **food waste**.

Together with the World Health Organization, the FAO publishes the **Codex Alimentarius**. This is a collection of standards for safe food, for example on limits and labelling. Many countries base their own food laws on it. This also makes the worldwide trade in food safer.

Switzerland is a member of the FAO and supports projects for sustainable farming and food security. The FAO should not be confused with the **World Food Programme** (WFP), which is also based in Rome and mainly hands out food in emergencies. The WFP received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020. In Switzerland, too, schools and the media draw attention to hunger and food waste on World Food Day.

begriffe.erklaerung: Everyone has enough healthy food at all times.
The body does not get enough food over a long period.
Food that is thrown away or lost.
A collection of international rules for safe food.

gewusst: Until 1951 the FAO was based in Washington before it moved to Rome.
At the FAO headquarters in Rome there stood an obelisk from Ethiopia, which was returned to Ethiopia in 2005 after decades in Rome.

t1mbu3ie.t: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties

teile.einleitung: The Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties governs how treaties between states are made, how they apply and how they are interpreted. In German it is called the WVK for short. It is, so to speak, a treaty about treaties.
wichtigste: The Convention was adopted in Vienna in 1969 and came into force in 1980.
Art. 26 contains the principle “pacta sunt servanda”: treaties must be kept.
Under Art. 27 a state may not rely on its own law to break a treaty.
Treaties are interpreted according to their wording, context, and object and purpose.
A treaty obtained by force is void.
With a reservation a state can exclude certain provisions for itself.

abschnitte.text: States conclude many treaties, for example on trade, borders or environmental protection. The **Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties** sets out the rules that apply to such treaties. It was adopted in Vienna on **22 May 1969** and opened for signature the next day. It only came into force on **27 January 1980**. It applies to written treaties between states. Switzerland is also a party.

The most important principle is in **Art. 26**: **pacta sunt servanda**, Latin for “treaties must be kept”. Every valid treaty binds the parties and must be carried out in **good faith**. Under **Art. 27** a state may not use its **domestic law** as an excuse for not carrying out a treaty. This even applies to its constitution, with a narrow exception in Art. 46.

Under **Art. 7**, **heads of state**, **heads of government** and **foreign ministers** count as representatives of their state by virtue of their office. They do not need full powers. If a state has signed a treaty but not yet ratified it, under **Art. 18** it may not defeat the object and purpose of the treaty. With a **reservation** a state can exclude certain provisions for itself. But reservations are not allowed if they are incompatible with the object and purpose of the treaty.

Sometimes states do not agree on what a treaty means. **Art. 31** says how to **interpret** it: in good faith, according to the ordinary meaning of the words in their context and in the light of its **object and purpose**. The preparatory work, that is drafts and records of the negotiations, are only supplementary means under Art. 32.

Under **Art. 52** a treaty obtained by the **threat or use of force** against a state is **void**. This rule is linked to the ban on the use of force in the UN Charter. Under **Art. 62** a **fundamental change of circumstances** can only exceptionally lead to a treaty ending. This principle is called **clausula rebus sic stantibus**. It is excluded for boundary treaties.

gewusst: Many rules of the Convention already counted as customary law beforehand and therefore also bind states that have not joined it.
The principle “pacta sunt servanda” is much older than the Convention and is one of the oldest rules of international law.

teile.einleitung: A sceptre is a decorated staff carried by kings and emperors as a sign of their power. Together with the crown and the orb, it is one of the most important symbols of rule. The sceptres of the British Crown Jewels are especially famous.
wichtigste: A sceptre is a ruler's staff and a sign of power.
At great ceremonies the king holds the sceptre in his hand.
The crown, sceptre and orb are among the symbols of a ruler.
The diamond “Cullinan I” is set in the British Sceptre with the Cross.
Another British coronation sceptre has a dove on top.

abschnitte.text: The word **sceptre** comes from the Greek word for “staff”. Even in ancient times rulers carried a staff as a sign that they ruled. At great ceremonies such as a **coronation** the king holds the sceptre in his **hand**. That way everyone can see that he rules. Together with the **crown** and the **orb** it forms the most important **symbols of rule**. The orb is a golden ball with a cross on top.

The British **Crown Jewels** include two famous sceptres. The diamond **“Cullinan I”** is set in the **Sceptre with the Cross**. It is one of the largest cut diamonds in the world. On top of the **Sceptre with the Dove** sits a white **dove**. It is a sign of peace and of the Holy Spirit. At the coronation the new king is handed both sceptres.

Many sceptres are kept in treasuries today. The British Crown Jewels are in the **Tower of London** and can be seen there. The treasury in **Vienna** holds the insignia of the former Holy Roman Empire, including a sceptre. Countries without a king, such as Switzerland, do not have such symbols of rule.

gewusst: The Cullinan diamond was found in South Africa in 1905 and was the largest rough diamond ever discovered.
At his coronation in 2023, King Charles III held both British sceptres in his hands.

teile.einleitung: The Treaty of Lisbon is the treaty that shapes the European Union today. It was signed in Lisbon in 2007 and has applied since 2009. It gave the EU new offices, more citizens' rights and, for the first time, a rule for leaving.
wichtigste: The treaty was signed in Lisbon in December 2007.
It came into force on 1 December 2009.
It replaced the failed EU constitution.
Since then Article 50 has governed a country's withdrawal.
The Charter of Fundamental Rights became legally binding.
The permanent President of the European Council and the High Representative are new.
A European Citizens' Initiative needs one million signatures.

abschnitte.text: In **2005** **France** and the **Netherlands** rejected the planned **EU constitution** in referendums. Much of its content was then taken over into a new treaty. This was signed in **December 2007** in **Lisbon**, the capital of **Portugal**. Portugal held the Council presidency at the time. After all the countries had approved it, the treaty came into force on **1 December 2009**.

The treaty created the office of a **permanent President of the European Council**. The first holder of the office, from **2009 to 2014**, was the Belgian **Herman Van Rompuy**. Before that the presidency changed every six months. The **High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy** is also new. This person leads the EU's foreign policy and is at the same time **Vice-President of the Commission**. The role is often called the EU's foreign policy chief.

The **Charter of Fundamental Rights** has existed since 2000. Since the Treaty of Lisbon it has been just as **binding** as the EU treaties. In addition, the EU as a whole gained its own **legal personality**. It can therefore conclude international agreements itself. The **European Citizens' Initiative** is also new: with **one million signatures** from at least **seven** countries, citizens can ask the Commission to propose a law.

Since 2014 the **double majority** has applied for a **qualified majority** in the Council. A decision needs at least **55 per cent** of the member states, together representing at least **65 per cent** of the EU population. For the first time the treaty also governs a country's **withdrawal**, namely in **Article 50** of the EU Treaty. The **United Kingdom** used this article for **Brexit**.

gewusst: Before the Treaty of Lisbon there was no rule at all in the EU treaties on how a country could leave.
The United Kingdom was the first country to leave the EU using Article 50.

teile.einleitung: The UN Security Council is the most powerful body of the United Nations. It is responsible for keeping peace and security in the world. Unlike the General Assembly, it can make decisions that all states must follow.
wichtigste: The Security Council has 15 members: 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent.
The five permanent members are the USA, Russia, China, France and the United Kingdom.
Each permanent member has a right of veto and can block a resolution on its own.
The non-permanent members are elected for two years by the General Assembly.
The Security Council can decide on sanctions and send peace missions.
Switzerland was a member for the first time in 2023 and 2024.
Reform is often discussed because the membership no longer reflects today's world.

abschnitte.text: According to the UN Charter, the **Security Council** has the main responsibility for world peace. It meets when there are wars or dangerous conflicts and can call on the opposing sides to make peace. It can decide on **sanctions**, for example an arms embargo or freezing money. In the most extreme case it may even allow military force. It also sends peacekeeping troops, the so-called Blue Helmets, to crisis areas.

The five permanent members are the USA, Russia, China, France and the United Kingdom, the most important victorious powers of the Second World War. In 1991 Russia took over the seat of the Soviet Union. Until 1971 China's seat was held by the Republic of China on Taiwan, then it passed to the People's Republic of China. In addition there are ten **non-permanent members**, each elected for two years. The Council has had 15 seats since 1965; before that there were 11.

A decision needs at least nine votes in favour. But each permanent member can block a resolution on its own with its **veto**. This often means the Council cannot act in major conflicts, for example when a permanent member is itself involved. Since 2022 the General Assembly meets after every veto to debate it.

Many states think the Council shows the world of 1945 and not the world of today. Africa and Latin America, for example, have no permanent seat. India, Brazil, Germany and Japan would like a permanent seat and work together for this as the **G4**. But **reform** is difficult because the Charter would have to be changed and the permanent members would have to agree.

In 2022 Switzerland was elected to the Council by a large majority for the years 2023 and 2024. It held the **presidency**, which changes every month, in May 2023 and October 2024. Among other things, Switzerland worked for the protection of civilians and for climate security. Before it stood as a candidate, there was debate about whether a seat was compatible with neutrality.

begriffe.erklaerung: Latin for “I forbid”. A single no that prevents a decision.
A penalty, for example a trade ban, to put pressure on a country.
Soldiers of the UN peacekeeping forces, named after their light blue helmets.
A country that always sits on the Council and never has to be re-elected.

gewusst: Over the course of history, the Soviet Union and Russia have used the veto most often.
On the Security Council the presidency changes every month, in turn according to the English alphabetical order of the countries' names.

teile.einleitung: Rubbish is produced every day: paper, glass, bottles and food scraps. In Switzerland the **municipality** collects many kinds of waste separately so that they can be recycled.
wichtigste: Recycling means that old things are used again.
Used glass is sorted by colour: clear, brown and green.
Empty batteries are taken back to the shop.
Peelings such as carrot peel go in the green waste.
Littering means carelessly throwing rubbish away.
Bulky waste such as an old sofa is taken to the municipal depot or waste collection centre.

abschnitte.text: Many things can be used again. This is called **recycling**: old bottles become new bottles and waste paper becomes new paper. This means fewer new raw materials and less energy are needed. Anything that cannot be recycled goes in the **rubbish bag**. In many municipalities you have to pay a fee for this bag.

Empty **glass bottles** are taken to the **bottle bank**. There are containers there for **clear, brown and green** glass. On **Sundays** and late in the evening you do not throw glass in, because it clinks loudly and disturbs the neighbours. Empty **PET bottles** go in the PET collection, which almost every shop has. You squash them flat first and screw the lid back on.

You bundle up **waste paper** and tie it together with **string**. Then you put it out by the road on collection day. Peelings such as **carrot peel**, apple cores or grass go in the **green waste**, which is turned into compost or biogas. Empty **batteries** are taken back to the shop, because shops that sell batteries take them back. Batteries never belong in the rubbish.

Large items such as an old sofa are called **bulky waste**. In many municipalities you can hand them in at the **municipal depot** or **waste collection centre**. Anyone who simply throws rubbish on the ground is **littering**. This is bad for animals and nature and makes a lot of work for those who clean up. In many places littering can be punished with a fine.

gewusst: Switzerland is one of the countries that recycle an especially large amount of glass and PET.
What ends up in the rubbish bag is usually burnt in a waste incineration plant, which turns it into electricity and heat.

teile.einleitung: Anyone who lives in Switzerland without a Swiss passport needs a **foreign nationals' permit**. It shows how long and for what purpose someone may be here. Each permit has a letter, for example B, C or L.
wichtigste: Permit B is the temporary residence permit.
Permit C is the permanent settlement permit.
Permit L is for short stays, usually of less than a year.
Asylum seekers receive permit N during the procedure, and provisionally admitted people permit F.
From 2022 refugees from Ukraine received protection status S.
The cantonal migration offices grant the permits.

abschnitte.titel: B and C: living and staying
abschnitte.text: **Permit B** is the residence permit. It is given to people who live in Switzerland for a longer period, for example because of a job. It is **temporary** and must be renewed regularly. For citizens of EU and EFTA states it is valid for five years. **Permit C** is the settlement permit and is valid **without time limit**. You usually receive it after ten years, or after five years if you are especially well integrated or a citizen of certain states.

abschnitte.titel: L and G: short stays or across the border
abschnitte.text: **Permit L** is the short-term residence permit. It is valid for temporary stays, usually less than a year. This applies, for example, to seasonal workers. **Permit G** is for **cross-border commuters**. They live abroad and work in Switzerland. They return regularly to where they live.

abschnitte.titel: N, F and S: seeking protection
abschnitte.text: Anyone who makes an **asylum application** in Switzerland receives **permit N**. It is valid until a decision has been made on the application. **Permit F** is for provisionally admitted people. It would not be reasonable to send them away, for example because of war in their home country. **Protection status S** was activated for the first time in March 2022. It allowed people from **Ukraine** to stay quickly without a regular asylum procedure.

The permits are granted by the **cantonal migration offices**. At federal level the **State Secretariat for Migration**, SEM for short, is responsible. It sets the rules and decides on asylum applications. Which permit is possible depends very much on a person's **nationality**. For people from the EU the Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons applies; for other countries stricter rules apply.

gewusst: Foreign nationals' permits today are the size of a credit card.
Permit C is an important requirement for becoming naturalised in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: In 1994 the Swiss people said yes to the **Alpine Initiative**. It calls for goods to be transported through the Alps by rail instead of by lorry. For many people the result was a surprise.
wichtigste: The people approved the Alpine Initiative in 1994.
The yes vote was around 52 per cent, with a turnout of around 41 per cent.
Goods transit traffic through the Alps is to go by rail.
The initiative allowed ten years for the shift.
The Federal Council recommended rejecting it; the transport minister was Adolf Ogi.
French-speaking Switzerland clearly rejected the initiative.

abschnitte.text: The **Alpine Initiative** aimed to protect the Alpine region from the effects of transit traffic. **Goods transit traffic** from border to border is to go by **rail**. It allowed **ten years** for this shift. In addition, the **capacity of the transit roads** in the Alpine region was not to be increased any further. So new motorways through the Alps are ruled out.

On 20 February 1994 around **52 per cent** of voters said yes. **Turnout** was around 41 per cent. A majority of the cantons also said yes. The **Federal Council** had recommended **rejecting** it. The transport minister at the time was Federal Councillor **Adolf Ogi**, who was campaigning for new railway tunnels to be built through the Alps.

The result showed a clear difference between the parts of the country. **French-speaking Switzerland** clearly rejected the initiative. In German-speaking Switzerland, and especially in the mountain cantons along the transit routes, there were many yes votes. The canton of Uri, through which the Gotthard route runs, said yes most clearly.

The content of the initiative is now in the **Federal Constitution**. To achieve the shift, Switzerland introduced the **heavy vehicle charge** for lorries and built new railway tunnels with the NRLA. The goal of the shift has still not been fully achieved. But a large share of the goods passing through the Swiss Alps already travels by rail.

gewusst: The Alpine Initiative is one of the few popular initiatives that have been approved.
At the time the result of the vote also caused a stir in the neighbouring countries.

teile.einleitung: A **voting date** is the day on which a vote is held. In Switzerland these Sundays are known long in advance. This way everyone can prepare well.
wichtigste: A voting date is the day on which a vote is held.
The Confederation sets the dates for national votes.
There is often a date in November, but never in July.
On one date people often vote on several proposals.
If no proposal is ready, the date is dropped.
You receive the papers a few weeks beforehand.

abschnitte.text: The **Confederation** sets the voting dates, and does so years in advance. Normally there are four dates a year: in spring, in early summer, in autumn and often in **November**. There is no voting date in **July**, because many people are away on their summer holidays then. Votes are always held on a **Sunday**.

On one voting Sunday people often vote on **several proposals**. These can be popular initiatives, referendums or changes to the constitution. If **no proposal is ready** for a date, it is simply dropped. **Municipalities** and **cantons** also often hold votes on their own questions on the same Sunday. This way people do not have to go to the polls so often.

The voting papers are sent to your home **a few weeks** before the vote. This leaves enough time to find out about the issues and decide calmly. You can vote by post or go to the polling station on voting day. What matters is that your vote arrives in time.

gewusst: Switzerland votes more often than almost any other country in the world.
There are separate dates for elections: the National Council is elected every four years in October.

teile.einleitung: A vice-president is the deputy of the president. In many countries this person steps in if the head of state is unable to serve. The office is especially well known in the USA, but Switzerland also has a Vice-President of the Federal Council.
wichtigste: The vice-president represents the president and takes over their tasks when needed.
If the US president dies or resigns, the vice-president immediately becomes president.
In the USA the president and vice-president stand for election as a team.
The US vice-president is also President of the Senate.
JD Vance has been Vice-President of the USA since January 2025.
In 2021 Kamala Harris became the first female Vice-President of the USA.
In Switzerland the Vice-President of the Federal Council usually becomes President of the Confederation the following year.

abschnitte.text: The word “vice” comes from Latin and means “in place of”. A vice-president is therefore a **deputy**. They take over tasks when the president is ill, travelling or unable to act. Many states, clubs and companies have such deputies. This means an organisation can still act even when the boss is not available.

In the USA each party chooses a **team** of two people: one for president and one for vice-president. If the president dies or resigns, the vice-president immediately becomes the new president. This is set out exactly in the **Constitution**. The vice-president is also **President of the Senate**, one of the two chambers of the parliament. If a vote in the Senate is tied, he may decide it with his vote.

The president lives in the White House, but the vice-president does not. His official residence is a house in the grounds of the **Naval Observatory** in Washington. There the navy used to observe the stars in order to work out exact times and positions for shipping. The house is only a few kilometres from the White House.

Many vice-presidents later became president themselves. **Joe Biden** was vice-president from 2009 to 2017 and president from 2021 to 2025. **Kamala Harris** became the first woman in this office in 2021. Since January 2025 **JD Vance** has been vice-president under President Donald Trump. Even the very first vice-president, John Adams, later became president.

Switzerland does not have a single head of state but a **Federal Council** with seven members. Every year the Federal Assembly elects one of them as **President of the Confederation** and one as **Vice-President**. It is the custom that the Vice-President becomes President the following year. So the office changes every year. The President chairs the meetings of the Federal Council but has no more power than the other members.

gewusst: Gerald Ford became President of the USA in 1974 without ever having been elected president or vice-president. He had moved up to become vice-president and then took over after Richard Nixon resigned.
John Adams, the first Vice-President of the USA, once called his office the most insignificant ever invented.

teile.einleitung: The World Trade Organization, WTO for short, sets rules for international trade. It makes sure that countries can exchange goods and services with each other fairly. It is based in Geneva, and almost all the countries of the world are members.
wichtigste: The WTO sets rules for international trade.
It is based in Geneva, in the Centre William Rappard on Lake Geneva.
It was founded on 1 January 1995.
Before that, the GATT trade agreement had existed since 1947.
The WTO has about 166 members (as of 2025).
It helps to settle trade disputes between countries peacefully.
Switzerland has been a member since it was founded.

abschnitte.text: The abbreviation WTO comes from the English name **World Trade Organization**. It is an international organisation in which countries negotiate common rules for trade. These concern, for example, **customs duties**, which are fees on imported goods. The aim is for trade between countries to be as free, fair and predictable as possible.

As early as 1947 several countries concluded the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, **GATT** for short. It was meant to get trade going again after the Second World War. After long negotiations the WTO was founded on 1 January 1995 and took over the tasks of the GATT. China joined in 2001, Russia in 2012.

The member states usually make their decisions together by **consensus**, meaning only when nobody is against. About every two years there is a Ministerial Conference, the WTO's most important meeting. An important principle is that advantages one country grants to a trading partner must in principle be granted to all members. The WTO is led by a Director-General; since 2021 this has been Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala from Nigeria.

When two countries argue about trade rules, they can use the WTO's **dispute settlement procedure**. Experts then examine who has kept to the rules. This is meant to stop countries simply putting high customs duties on each other. Since 2019, however, the Appellate Body has been blocked because the USA is preventing the appointment of new members.

Switzerland is a small country that exports a great deal, for example medicines, machines, watches and chocolate. That is why fixed trade rules are especially important for it. It was already part of the GATT and has been a member of the WTO since 1995. The headquarters in **Geneva** also bring many diplomats and experts to the city.

begriffe.erklaerung: A fee you have to pay when goods are brought across a national border.
Selling goods abroad.
Buying goods from abroad.
The trade agreement of 1947 from which the WTO developed.

gewusst: The WTO building in Geneva, the Centre William Rappard, used to be the seat of the International Labour Office.
Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is the first woman and the first person from Africa to head the WTO.
Regions such as Hong Kong and the European Union are also independent members of the WTO.

teile.einleitung: **Alexis de Tocqueville** was a French thinker, historian and politician of the 19th century. After a journey through the USA he wrote a famous book about democracy. His ideas are still read today.
wichtigste: Alexis de Tocqueville lived from 1805 to 1859.
His best-known work is called “Democracy in America”.
The official reason for his journey to the USA in 1831 was to study the prison system.
At the centre of his thinking is equality of conditions.
He warned against the tyranny of the majority.
In 1849 he was briefly French foreign minister.

abschnitte.text: Tocqueville came from a noble French family. In 1831 he travelled to the USA with his friend **Gustave de Beaumont**. The official reason was to **study the prison system**, because American prisons were considered modern at the time. But Tocqueville was mainly interested in how the young **democracy** worked. The two travelled through the country for about nine months.

His best-known work is called **“Democracy in America”**. It appeared in two parts, in 1835 and 1840. At its centre he put **equality of conditions**: in America there was no nobility as in Europe, and people met each other on much more equal terms. Tocqueville was convinced that this development would also win through in Europe.

Tocqueville also saw dangers. He warned especially against the **tyranny of the majority**: the majority could oppress minorities and silence differing opinions. He also feared a new, **soft despotism**. In it the state would guide citizens like a patronising guardian instead of letting them decide for themselves. As a counterweight to isolation he praised **voluntary associations**, in which citizens achieve things together.

In France Tocqueville was a member of parliament. In 1849 he was **foreign minister** for a few months. After Louis Napoléon's coup in 1851 he withdrew from politics. In his late work **“The Old Regime and the Revolution”** of 1856 he examined the causes of the **French Revolution**. He showed that much of what the Revolution brought had already begun in the old kingdom.

gewusst: Tocqueville was elected to the Académie française in 1841.
His book about America is still read at many universities today, including in the USA itself.

teile.einleitung: The UNHCR is the UN Refugee Agency. It protects people who have had to flee their homes because of war, violence or persecution. Its headquarters are in Geneva, and it has already received the Nobel Peace Prize twice.
wichtigste: The main task of the UNHCR is to protect and support refugees worldwide.
UNHCR stands for “United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees”.
The UNHCR was founded in 1950 and is based in Geneva.
Its work is based on the Geneva Refugee Convention of 1951.
The agency received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and 1981.
In 2025 well over 100 million people worldwide had been forced to flee.
The UNHCR provides refugees with tents, water and food and helps them build a new life.

abschnitte.text: The **UNHCR** was created by the UN General Assembly on 14 December 1950 and began work in 1951. Originally it was only meant to help refugees from the Second World War in Europe for a few years. But because new crises kept arising, it became a permanent organisation. Today it works in over 130 countries. It is led by the UN **High Commissioner for Refugees**.

The **Geneva Refugee Convention** of 1951 sets out who counts as a refugee. A refugee is a person who is persecuted because of their origin, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership of a group. The most important principle is called **non-refoulement**: nobody may be sent back to a country where they face persecution. The UNHCR makes sure that states keep to these rules.

When many people flee at once, the UNHCR sets up **refugee camps**. It hands out tents, blankets, drinking water and hygiene items and provides medical help. It also helps children in the camps to go to school. However, many refugees do not live in camps but in towns and cities in neighbouring countries.

The UNHCR looks for three possible solutions for refugees. The first is voluntary return when it is safe at home again. The second is integration in the host country. The third is **resettlement** in another country that takes in especially vulnerable people, as Switzerland also does.

The UNHCR's headquarters are in Geneva, very close to other UN buildings. Switzerland is an important donor and works closely with the agency. In Switzerland the State Secretariat for Migration examines whether someone receives asylum. Another well-known figure is **Sadruddin Aga Khan**, who was High Commissioner for Refugees from 1965 to 1977 and lived for a long time on Lake Geneva.

begriffe.erklaerung: A person who has had to leave their home because they are persecuted or threatened there.
Protection that a state grants to a persecuted person.
The ban on sending someone back to a country where they face danger.
People who have had to flee within their own country.

gewusst: About 40 per cent of all people who have been forced to flee are children.
Every year the UNHCR awards the Nansen Refugee Award, named after the Norwegian polar explorer Fridtjof Nansen, who already helped refugees for the League of Nations.

teile.einleitung: The World Food Programme, WFP for short, is a UN organisation that fights hunger. It brings food to people in need, for example after disasters or in war zones. In 2020 it received the Nobel Peace Prize.
wichtigste: The WFP fights hunger above all.
It was founded in 1961 and has its headquarters in Rome.
In 2020 the WFP received the Nobel Peace Prize.
It is funded by voluntary contributions from states, companies and private individuals.
Some families receive money or vouchers instead of food.
The WFP brings food to areas without roads by plane and helicopter.

abschnitte.text: The **World Food Programme** (WFP) is the largest humanitarian organisation fighting hunger. It was founded in **1961** and began its work two years later. Its headquarters are in **Rome**, the capital of Italy. The WFP helps in emergencies and supports communities so that they can later provide for themselves.

After **earthquakes**, **floods** or in **wars**, people often suddenly have nothing left to eat. Then the WFP quickly brings food. Where no roads lead, it flies in aid supplies with **planes** and **helicopters**. Sometimes sacks of food are even dropped from the plane. Sacks and lorries are usually white and carry the blue logo so that they are easy to recognise.

The WFP does not always hand out sacks of rice or flour. Where there is enough food at the market, families receive **money** or **vouchers**. That way they can buy what they need themselves. Local traders earn money too, and that helps the whole area. For small children there is especially nourishing **special food** with many vitamins and minerals.

The WFP has no fixed budget from compulsory contributions. It depends on **voluntary contributions** from states, companies and private individuals. Switzerland also supports the WFP. When less money comes in, the programme sometimes has to cut food rations. That is why it keeps calling for donations.

In **2020** the WFP received the **Nobel Peace Prize**. The Nobel Committee praised its work against hunger. It also stressed that hunger and war are closely linked: war often leads to hunger, and hunger can make conflicts worse. So anyone who fights hunger also helps peace.

gewusst: The WFP runs its own air service for humanitarian aid workers.
In many countries the WFP hands out school meals so that children can learn on a full stomach and like coming to school.

teile.einleitung: The World Intellectual Property Organization, WIPO for short, is a specialised agency of the UN based in Geneva. It works worldwide to protect inventions, brands and creative works. Its roots are in Bern.
wichtigste: WIPO is based in Geneva.
Intellectual property means rights to inventions, brands and works.
The WIPO Convention was signed in Stockholm in 1967 and came into force in 1970.
Its forerunner BIRPI was in Bern until 1960.
WIPO administers the Berne Convention of 1886 and the Paris Convention of 1883.
26 April is World Intellectual Property Day.
In the Global Innovation Index 2025 Switzerland came first.

abschnitte.text: Not only things like a bike can belong to someone, but also ideas and creative work. This is called **intellectual property**. A **patent** protects an invention from being copied for a certain time. A **trade mark** protects a name or a logo. **Copyright** protects works such as books, music or pictures. Anyone who invents or creates something should be able to benefit from it.

Already in the 19th century, states concluded agreements to protect intellectual property. The **Paris Convention** of 1883 protects patents, trade marks and designs. The **Berne Convention** of 1886 protects works of literature and art. The agreements were administered by the **BIRPI** office in **Bern**. In 1960 the office moved to **Geneva** and later became WIPO.

The **Convention Establishing WIPO** was signed in **Stockholm** in **1967**. It came into force on **26 April 1970**. That is why 26 April is now **World Intellectual Property Day**. Since 1974 WIPO has been a **specialised agency of the UN**. Today it administers numerous international treaties.

A patent or a trade mark actually only applies in the country where it is registered. WIPO therefore offers systems with which you can reach many countries at once. With the **Madrid System** you submit a single application and can have a trade mark protected in many member countries. For inventions there is a similar procedure for patent applications. This saves time and money.

Every year WIPO publishes the **Global Innovation Index**. It compares how innovative countries are, meaning how well they develop and use new ideas. In the 2025 index **Switzerland** came **first**, as it had in many years before. In Switzerland the **Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property** in Bern is responsible for patents and trade marks.

gewusst: The Berne Convention of 1886 is named after the Swiss capital and today applies in almost every country in the world.
Copyright comes into being automatically as soon as a work is created. You do not have to register it.

teile.einleitung: Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean. Since 1974 it has been divided into a Greek Cypriot south and a Turkish Cypriot north. This dispute is called the **Cyprus dispute**.
wichtigste: Cyprus became independent from Britain in 1960.
In 1974 Turkey occupied the north of the island.
The north declared itself a state in 1983, but only Turkey recognises it.
The capital Nicosia is divided.
UN peacekeeping troops monitor the buffer zone between north and south.
In 2004 the Greek Cypriots rejected the Annan Plan.
Cyprus has been a member of the EU since 2004.

abschnitte.text: From 1878 Cyprus was under **British administration** and later became a crown colony. Greek and Turkish Cypriots lived on the island. In 1960 Cyprus became **independent**. However, Britain kept two military bases, which still exist today. Soon there were serious tensions between the two communities, and so UN troops came to the island in 1964.

In 1974 Greek nationalist officers staged a coup. They wanted to unite Cyprus with **Greece**. In response, troops from **Turkey** landed and occupied the north of the island. Many people had to leave their homes and move to the other side. In 1983 the north declared itself the **Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus**. Apart from Turkey, no state recognises this republic; internationally the area is regarded as part of the Republic of Cyprus.

A **buffer zone**, also called the Green Line, runs across the island. It goes right through the capital **Nicosia**, which is therefore divided. The UN mission **UNFICYP** monitors this zone. It has been on the island since 1964 and is one of the UN's oldest peacekeeping missions. Since 2003 there have been crossing points where people can go back and forth between the two parts.

For decades the UN has been trying to reunite the island. In 2004 both communities voted on the **Annan Plan**, named after the UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan. A majority of Turkish Cypriots said yes, but around three quarters of Greek Cypriots said no. So the plan failed. In 2017 the parties negotiated in **Crans-Montana** in the canton of Valais, but these talks also ended without agreement.

On 1 May 2004 Cyprus joined the **European Union** together with nine other countries. Formally the whole island belongs to it. In the north, however, **EU law** is suspended for as long as the conflict is not resolved. The Republic of Cyprus pays with the euro; in the north the Turkish lira is widely used.

gewusst: Nicosia is regarded as the last divided capital in Europe.
The UN mission in Cyprus has existed since 1964, which is more than 60 years.

teile.einleitung: The two per cent target is a NATO guideline. Member states are to spend at least two per cent of their gross domestic product on defence every year. In 2025 NATO agreed a new, higher target.
wichtigste: The two per cent target was set down at the NATO summit in Wales in 2014.
It refers to gross domestic product, the economic output of a country.
The states were to move towards the target by 2024.
20 per cent of defence spending is to go on major equipment and on research and development.
In 2025 in The Hague NATO agreed a target of 5 per cent of GDP by 2035.
In 2022 Germany created a special fund of 100 billion euros for its armed forces.

abschnitte.text: **NATO** is a defence alliance of states from Europe and North America. Its members have agreed to spend at least **two per cent** of their **gross domestic product** (GDP) on defence every year. GDP is the value of all the goods and services a country produces in one year. So if the economy grows, the amount needed to meet the target also rises.

In September **2014** the NATO states met in Newport in **Wales**. In the summit declaration they set down the two per cent target. The background was Russia's **annexation of Crimea** in the same year. The states committed themselves to moving towards the guideline within a decade, that is **by 2024**. In addition, at least **20 per cent** of spending is to go on major weapons systems and on research and development.

After Russia's attack on **Ukraine** in February 2022, many states greatly increased their spending. **Germany** created a **special fund** of **100 billion euros** for the Bundeswehr, its armed forces. It was anchored in the Basic Law, Germany's constitution, and is meant to help modernise equipment. According to NATO estimates, **Poland** had the highest share in 2024, at around 4.1 per cent of GDP. Poland is arming heavily because it is close to Russia and Belarus.

At the NATO summit in **The Hague** in **2025**, the members agreed a new target. By **2035** they are to spend **5 per cent** of their GDP. Of this, **3.5 per cent** is planned for defence itself and **1.5 per cent** for related areas such as infrastructure and resilience. The new target replaces the previous guideline. Whether all states will reach it is disputed.

**Switzerland** is neutral and not a member of NATO. The two per cent target therefore does not apply to it. But in Switzerland, too, there is debate about how much money the **army** should receive. Parliament has decided to increase army spending step by step. Supporters point to the uncertain situation in Europe, opponents to other important tasks of the Confederation.

gewusst: The two per cent guideline existed in NATO before 2014, but at the Wales summit it was set down by the heads of state and government for the first time.
NATO's new target of 5 per cent is more than twice as high as the old two per cent target.

teile.einleitung: **Voting Sunday** is the day on which the people in Switzerland decide on proposals. Normally there are four such dates a year. Preparations begin weeks beforehand.
wichtigste: National votes normally take place on four dates a year.
The Federal Council decides which proposals are put to the people.
The papers must arrive at least three weeks before voting day.
The great majority vote by post.
In most municipalities the polls close at 12 noon.
The municipalities' electoral offices count the votes.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland national votes normally take place on **four dates** a year. The **Federal Council** decides which proposals are put to the people on a voting Sunday. Often there are several at once. On the same day, cantons and municipalities often also vote on their own proposals.

Voters must receive their papers **at least three weeks** before voting day. They include the ballot paper, the voting card and the Federal Council's booklet, the **voting explanations**. In it the proposals are explained, and supporters and opponents have their say. Today the great majority of voters vote **by post**.

Anyone who does not vote by post goes to the polling station and puts the ballot paper in the **ballot box**. In most municipalities the polls close at **12 noon**. An envelope sent by post only counts if it reaches the municipality **before the polls close**. After that the municipalities' **electoral offices** begin counting.

In the afternoon television publishes a **projection**. This is an estimate of the result based on partial results. One by one the cantons report their results. By the evening the result is usually certain. The Federal Council then gives information at a press conference.

gewusst: The voting dates are set by the Confederation many years in advance.
Some voters deliberately go to the polling station on Sunday morning because they like this tradition.

teile.einleitung: The USMCA is a free trade agreement between the USA, Mexico and Canada. It has been in force since 2020 and replaced the older NAFTA agreement. Together the three countries form a large economic area in North America.
wichtigste: The USMCA includes the USA, Mexico and Canada.
It came into force on 1 July 2020.
It replaced the NAFTA agreement, which had applied since 1994.
In Mexico it is called T-MEC, in Canada CUSMA.
Strict rules apply to cars: around 75 per cent of their value must come from the region.
The three states review the agreement every six years.

abschnitte.text: A **free trade agreement** lowers or removes **customs duties** on goods between the partner countries. A customs duty is a fee that has to be paid when goods cross a border. Without customs duties, goods from the partner country become cheaper. A **common currency** or open borders for people are not part of a free trade agreement. Switzerland also has many free trade agreements, for example with the EU.

The **North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA)** came into force on **1 January 1994**. At the time it created one of the largest free trade areas in the world. In **2017** the three countries began to negotiate a new agreement. The **USMCA** came into force on **1 July 2020** and replaced NAFTA. The name stands for “United States, Mexico, Canada Agreement”.

Each country calls the agreement something slightly different. In the USA it is called the **USMCA**. In **Mexico** people say **T-MEC**, short for “Tratado entre México, Estados Unidos y Canadá”. In **Canada** it is called **CUSMA**. In all three names the country's own name comes first.

The **rules of origin** for the **car industry** are especially important. For a car to be traded free of customs duties, around **75 per cent** of its value must come from North America. This is meant to secure jobs in the region. The agreement also contains rules on **workers' rights** and on trade over the internet. Every **six years** the three states must **review** the agreement together; the first review was scheduled for July 2026.

gewusst: Goods worth billions of dollars are traded between the three USMCA countries every day.
Many car parts cross borders in North America several times on their way to becoming a finished car.

t3gogjv.t: Term of office of the Federal Council

teile.einleitung: The seven members of the **Federal Council** are elected by the United Federal Assembly for four years. Re-election is allowed, and there is no limit on the number of terms. So many federal councillors stay in office for a long time.
wichtigste: The Federal Council is elected again every four years after the parliamentary elections.
The four years between two general elections are called a legislative period.
There is no age limit or limit on terms of office.
On average, members of the Federal Council stay in office for around ten years.
Up to 2026 a sitting member was not re-elected four times.
Karl Schenk had the longest term of office.

abschnitte.text: After the elections to the National Council a new **legislative period** of four years begins. At the start, the **United Federal Assembly**, that is the National Council and the Council of States together, elects the whole Federal Council again. Each member is elected individually. Anyone who stands again is usually **re-elected**. There is neither an **age limit** nor a limit on how often someone may be re-elected.

On average, members of the Federal Council stay in office for **around ten years**. The record is held by **Karl Schenk** from the canton of Bern. He was a federal councillor from 1864 to 1895, more than 30 years. Today most resign voluntarily. Their successor is then chosen in a **by-election**.

It is very rare for a sitting member not to be re-elected. Since 1848 it has happened **four times** (as of 2026). The first was **Ulrich Ochsenbein** in 1854. In 1872 it happened to Jean-Jacques Challet-Venel. In 2003 **Ruth Metzler** was not re-elected, and in 2007 **Christoph Blocher**. Both removals caused a great stir throughout Switzerland.

gewusst: Karl Schenk was President of the Confederation several times.
The President of the Confederation is elected anew from the Federal Council every year.

teile.einleitung: UNAIDS is the joint United Nations programme against HIV and AIDS. It coordinates the work of several UN organisations in this field. Its headquarters are in Geneva.
wichtigste: UNAIDS fights HIV and AIDS worldwide.
It was decided on in 1994 and has been working since 1996.
Its headquarters are in Geneva, close to the WHO.
Several UN organisations such as the WHO, UNICEF and UNDP work together in it.
World AIDS Day is on 1 December every year.
The red ribbon shows solidarity with people living with HIV.
UNAIDS wants to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.

abschnitte.text: **HIV** stands for “human immunodeficiency virus”, a virus that weakens the **immune system**. It attacks the body's defences, the so-called **immune system**. Without treatment, the disease **AIDS** can develop from it after some years. The body can then hardly defend itself against many illnesses. Today there are **medicines** that allow people with HIV to live long and well. So far, however, HIV cannot be cured.

UNAIDS was decided on in **1994** and began its work in **1996**. It took over tasks from an older programme of the **World Health Organization (WHO)**. What is special is that UNAIDS links several UN organisations. These **cosponsors** include, for example, the **WHO**, the children's fund **UNICEF** and the development programme **UNDP**. Together they are meant to tackle HIV more effectively.

UNAIDS has its headquarters in **Geneva**. The WHO, with which UNAIDS works closely, is also there. Geneva is an important place for global health policy. From here UNAIDS collects figures, advises governments and supports programmes in many countries. Countries in southern Africa are especially affected.

Since **1988**, **World AIDS Day** has been held on **1 December** every year. It remembers the people who have died of AIDS and calls for **solidarity**. Its well-known symbol is the **red ribbon**. It became known in **1991**. Anyone who wears it shows that people with HIV should not be excluded.

UNAIDS has set itself clear targets. The first “95” means that **95 per cent** of people with HIV know about their infection. The other targets concern **treatment** and a strongly suppressed **viral load**, meaning very few viruses in the body. The big goal is to end AIDS as a public health threat **by 2030**. It is part of the UN's **2030 Agenda**.

gewusst: People who are treated effectively often have so few viruses in their blood that they can no longer be measured with ordinary tests.
In Switzerland, the Swiss AIDS Federation (Aids-Hilfe Schweiz) has supported people with HIV since 1985.

teile.einleitung: World Environment Day takes place every year on 5 June. The UN declared it so that people all over the world think about protecting the environment. Each year there is a theme of its own and usually a host country.
wichtigste: World Environment Day is on 5 June.
It remembers the UN environment conference that began in Stockholm on 5 June 1972.
It was decided on in 1972 and first celebrated in 1974.
It is organised by the UN Environment Programme, UNEP for short.
Each year it has its own theme and usually a host country.
In 2018 India was the host, and the theme was directed against plastic.

abschnitte.text: On **5 June 1972** the first big environment conference of the **UN** began in **Stockholm** in Sweden. For the first time many states talked together there about environmental problems such as polluted air and polluted water. That same year the United Nations decided to celebrate **World Environment Day** every year on 5 June. It took place for the first time in **1974**.

Also in 1972 the UN founded its **environment programme**. Its English name is “United Nations Environment Programme”, **UNEP** for short. UNEP organises World Environment Day. In German the day is called **Weltumwelttag**, “Umwelt” being the German word for environment. UNEP is based in Nairobi, the capital of Kenya.

Each World Environment Day has its own **theme**. Usually a **host country** takes over the organisation of the most important events. In **2018** this was **India**. The theme was “Beat Plastic Pollution”. Other years were devoted, for example, to forests, oceans, air or the protection of soils.

On World Environment Day events take place all over the world. People collect litter, plant trees or give information about environmental problems. School classes also take part. The day is meant to show that everyone can do something for the environment, for example use less plastic and sort rubbish properly.

gewusst: World Environment Day is one of the UN's largest days of action and is marked in over 100 countries.
UNEP in Nairobi was the first UN organisation with its headquarters in a country of the Global South.

teile.einleitung: The Treaty of Nice is a reform treaty of the European Union. It was meant to prepare the EU for its big enlargement with many states from Central and Eastern Europe. It came into force in 2003.
wichtigste: The main aim was to prepare the institutions for enlargement.
The treaty was signed on 26 February 2001.
It came into force on 1 February 2003.
The four largest states received 29 votes each in the Council.
Ireland first said no and approved it in 2002.
Since 2004 each member state has provided only one commissioner.
The Charter of Fundamental Rights was proclaimed in Nice in 2000.

abschnitte.text: Many states from **Central and Eastern Europe** wanted to join the EU. With so many members, the way the institutions worked had to be adapted. At the summit in **Nice** in France in **December 2000** the governments agreed on reforms. The treaty was signed on **26 February 2001** and came into force on **1 February 2003**. Then in **2004** ten new states joined.

Nice reorganised the **weighting of votes** in the Council. **Germany**, **France**, **Italy** and the **United Kingdom** received **29 votes** each. **Spain** and **Poland** got **27 votes** each, even though they had far fewer inhabitants than Germany. This arrangement later became a **point of dispute**. The smallest country, **Malta**, had 3 votes.

Before, the five largest states each provided **two commissioners**. Since the **Barroso Commission**, which took office in **November 2004**, **each member state has provided one** commissioner. For the **European Parliament**, Nice set an upper limit of **732 members**. This number was later changed several times.

In **Ireland** voters first said **no** to the treaty in **June 2001**. After assurances about Irish **neutrality** they approved it in a second vote in **October 2002**. At the Nice summit the EU **Charter of Fundamental Rights** was also solemnly **proclaimed**. It had been drawn up by a **convention**, but only became legally binding some years later.

gewusst: The negotiations in Nice lasted several days and were among the longest EU summits.
Soon after Nice, work began on a bigger reform, the Constitutional Treaty.

teile.einleitung: Languages connect people, but they also differ from country to country. Switzerland has four national languages. And even in German, people in Switzerland, Germany and Austria say some things differently.
wichtigste: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
Romansh is spoken almost only in the canton of the Grisons.
In French you say “Bonjour” for “Good day” and “Au revoir” when leaving.
In Italian “thank you” is “Grazie”, and an ice cream is a “gelato”.
What is called a “Velo” (bicycle) in Switzerland is usually called a “Fahrrad” in Germany.
In Austria people say “Marille” for apricot and “Jänner” for January.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland has four **national languages**: **German**, **French**, **Italian** and **Romansh**. Most people speak German, often Swiss German in everyday life. French is spoken in western Switzerland, Italian mainly in Ticino. **Romansh** is spoken almost only in the canton of the **Grisons**, for example in the Engadine. It is the smallest of the four national languages.

In French you say **“Bonjour”** for “Good day”. When leaving you say **“Au revoir”**, which means “Goodbye”. **“Merci”** means “Thank you”, and **“S'il vous plaît”** means “Please”. Many French words are also known in Swiss German, for example “Merci” or “Trottoir” (pavement).

In Italian, “thank you” is **“Grazie”**. **“Prego”** means “You're welcome” or “Please”, and **“Ciao”** is used for “Hello” or “Bye”. An ice cream, which Swiss German calls a “Glace”, is a **“gelato”** in Italian. In Italy and in Ticino there are many gelaterias, which are ice cream shops. “Buongiorno” means “Good day”.

abschnitte.titel: German is not the same everywhere
abschnitte.text: German is spoken in several countries, but not the same way everywhere. For a bicycle, people in Switzerland say **“Velo”**, while in Germany they usually say **“Fahrrad”**. In **Austria** the apricot is called a **“Marille”**; apricot dumplings (“Marillenknödel”) are well known, for example. January is usually called **“Jänner”** there. Words that are typical of Switzerland are called **Helvetisms**. “Glace” (ice cream) and “Znüni” (a mid-morning snack) are among them too.

gewusst: There are several thousand languages in the world.
The word “Velo” comes from the French “vélocipède”.

teile.einleitung: The Security Council is the most powerful body of the United Nations (UN). It is meant to ensure peace and security in the world. All UN member states must follow its decisions.
wichtigste: The Security Council has 15 members.
Five of them are permanent members: the USA, Russia, China, France and the United Kingdom.
In addition there are 10 non-permanent members, each elected for two years.
Each permanent member has a veto and can use it to block decisions.
The Security Council can decide on sanctions and send peace missions.
It meets at the UN headquarters in New York.
In 2023 and 2024 Switzerland was a non-permanent member for the first time.

abschnitte.text: The Security Council is one of the six principal organs of the UN. It was founded in 1945 with the **Charter of the United Nations** and met for the first time in London in January 1946. Its most important task is maintaining world peace. Unlike the General Assembly, it can take decisions that are **binding** on all countries.

The five **permanent members** are the victorious powers of the Second World War: the USA, Russia, China, France and the United Kingdom. The 10 **non-permanent members** are elected by the General Assembly for two years, with half of them chosen anew each year. All regions of the world are meant to be represented, namely Africa, Asia, Latin America, Eastern Europe, and Western Europe and other states. Originally the Council had only 11 members; in 1965 it was enlarged to 15.

A decision, called a **resolution**, needs at least 9 votes in favour. On important questions, none of the five permanent members may vote against it. This power is called the **veto**. A single veto is enough to stop a resolution, even if all the others are in favour. That is why the Security Council is blocked in many conflicts, for example in the wars in Syria and Ukraine.

The Security Council can call on parties to a dispute to negotiate or lay down their weapons. It can impose **sanctions**, for example a ban on delivering weapons to a country. It can also send peacekeeping troops, who are called **blue helmets** because of their light blue helmets. In extreme cases it may even authorise military force. The presidency of the Council rotates among the members every month.

Switzerland has been a member of the UN since 2002. In June 2022 it was elected to the Security Council by the General Assembly for the first time. It sat there in 2023 and 2024 as a non-permanent member. Switzerland worked especially for the protection of civilians, for **international humanitarian law** and for climate protection. Beforehand many people asked whether this was compatible with neutrality; the Federal Council said it was.

Many countries think the Security Council no longer reflects today's world well. Africa and Latin America, for example, have no permanent seat. Countries such as Germany, Japan, India and Brazil would like a permanent seat themselves. But a **reform** would need the agreement of the five permanent members too, and that is why it has made no progress for decades.

begriffe.erklaerung: A decision that is voted on in the Security Council.
The right to block a decision with a single no vote.
Punitive measures against a country, for example trade bans.
UN soldiers who are meant to keep the peace in crisis areas.
A country that sits on the Security Council for only two years.

gewusst: In 1950 the Soviet Union stayed away from the meetings in protest and so could not veto the mission in the Korean War.
The council chamber in New York was a gift from Norway and is decorated with a large mural by the artist Per Krohg.
Non-permanent members may not be re-elected immediately after their two years.

teile.einleitung: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, SCO for short, is an association of countries mainly from Asia. They cooperate on security, the economy and politics. China and Russia are among its most important members.
wichtigste: The SCO was founded in Shanghai in 2001.
Its predecessor group was the “Shanghai Five” of 1996.
China and Russia are among the six founding states.
The secretariat is in Beijing.
India and Pakistan joined in 2017, Iran in 2023 and Belarus in 2024.
The official languages are Chinese and Russian.

abschnitte.text: In 1996 **China**, **Russia**, **Kazakhstan**, **Kyrgyzstan** and **Tajikistan** met. This group was called the **Shanghai Five**. They agreed on disarmament and **confidence-building measures** along the former Soviet-Chinese border. Confidence-building measures are agreements meant to reduce mistrust between neighbours, for example fewer soldiers at the border.

In **2001** the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation was founded in **Shanghai**. **Uzbekistan** joined the Shanghai Five. This made six founding states. Four of them are in **Central Asia**: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Although the organisation is named after Shanghai, its **secretariat** is in **Beijing**. Its counter-terrorism office is in **Tashkent**.

The SCO has grown over time. In **2017** **India** and **Pakistan** were admitted as full members. This took the organisation from six to eight members. In July **2023** **Iran** joined as the ninth member. In July **2024** **Belarus** was admitted at the summit in Astana. This means the organisation has ten members.

The **official languages** are **Chinese** and **Russian**, the languages of the two largest founding states. Besides the members there are observers and **dialogue partners**. **Turkey** has been a dialogue partner since 2012, even though it belongs to NATO. Mongolia is not a full member. The SCO is often described as a counterweight to Western alliances, but its members also pursue their own, sometimes differing aims.

gewusst: The SCO is named after Shanghai but has its secretariat in Beijing.
A very large part of the world's population lives in the SCO member states, because China and India belong to it.

teile.einleitung: The World Health Organization, WHO for short, is the United Nations organisation that looks after the health of people all over the world. Its headquarters are in Geneva in Switzerland. It helps in the fight against diseases and epidemics and gives advice on how people can stay healthy.
wichtigste: The WHO is the UN's World Health Organization.
Its headquarters are in Geneva.
It was founded on 7 April 1948, which is why 7 April is World Health Day.
Almost all the states of the world are members, about 194 countries.
The WHO helped to wipe out smallpox, which was officially declared in 1980.
In epidemics such as COVID-19 it coordinates worldwide cooperation.
Since 2017 Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus from Ethiopia has led the organisation.

abschnitte.text: The **World Health Organization** is a specialised agency of the United Nations. The abbreviation WHO comes from its English name. Its aim is for all people in the world to be able to live as healthily as possible. For the WHO, health does not just mean not being ill, but also feeling well in body, mind and in society.

The WHO was founded on 7 April 1948, shortly after the Second World War. To remember this, **World Health Day** is celebrated every year on 7 April. Even before that there were offices that dealt with epidemics, for example at the League of Nations in Geneva. The WHO took over these tasks and became much bigger.

One great success of the WHO was the worldwide vaccination campaign against **smallpox**. In 1980 the WHO declared this dangerous disease wiped out. Today, together with partners, it is fighting polio, which has almost disappeared. It also works against malaria, tuberculosis and HIV.

When a disease spreads very quickly across many countries, it is called a **pandemic**. In March 2020 the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic. In such cases it collects information, gives recommendations and helps poorer countries with supplies. In May 2025 the member states agreed on an accord so that the world is better prepared for future pandemics.

The WHO's headquarters are in **Geneva**, very close to other international organisations. Every year in May, representatives of the member states meet there for the **World Health Assembly**. They decide on the organisation's programme and money. Switzerland has been a member since 1947 and supports the WHO as host country. In 2025 the USA announced its withdrawal, which took effect at the beginning of 2026.

begriffe.erklaerung: A disease that spreads across many countries or even the whole world.
Protection that helps the body fight off a disease before you catch it.
The annual meeting of all WHO member states in Geneva.
An independent organisation that works with the UN and deals with a particular subject.

gewusst: Smallpox is the first human disease to have been completely wiped out by vaccination.
Switzerland joined the WHO as early as 1947, even though it only became a member of the UN in 2002.
The WHO keeps a list of essential medicines that should be available in every country.

teile.einleitung: On voting Sunday many people wait eagerly for the **voting result**. It shows how many yes and no votes there were and whether a proposal has been accepted or rejected.
wichtigste: The voting result shows how many yes and no votes there were.
At 60 per cent yes, more than half voted yes.
The result is usually known on Sunday afternoon or evening.
A projection is a first estimate before everything has been counted.
The official final result of a national vote is announced by the Confederation.
An accepted law only applies later, not that same evening.

abschnitte.text: The **voting result** shows how many **yes** and **no** votes there were. It is usually given in per cent. A result of 60 per cent yes means that more than half of the voters said yes. If a result is **close**, yes and no are near each other, for example at 50.5 to 49.5 per cent. For popular initiatives and changes to the constitution, a majority of the cantons, the **majority of the cantons**, is also needed.

On Sunday the polling stations usually close around midday. After that the municipalities count the votes. Soon there is a **projection** on television. This is a first estimate of the result before everything has been counted. The result is usually known on **Sunday afternoon** or in the **evening**.

Television often shows a **coloured map of Switzerland**. Each canton is coloured according to how it voted, for example green for yes and red for no. This way you can see at a glance where the proposal was popular and where it was not. After the vote a **member of the Federal Council** often comments on the result on television.

The official final result of a national vote is announced by the **Confederation**. The Federal Council checks the result and confirms it. However, an accepted new law does not apply on the evening of voting Sunday. It only comes into force **later**, often months afterwards. The date is usually set by the Federal Council.

gewusst: Only a few hours after the polls close, it is clear for most proposals how they will turn out.
If results are very close, there may be a recount in a municipality or a canton.

t991141.t: Voting rights for foreigners in Switzerland

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland normally only Swiss citizens may vote and stand in elections. In some municipalities and cantons, especially in French-speaking Switzerland, foreign nationals may also have a partial say. This is called voting rights for foreigners.
wichtigste: At federal level only Swiss citizens may vote and stand in elections.
In some municipalities in French-speaking Switzerland, foreigners may also vote.
The cantons of Jura and Neuchâtel even give foreigners voting rights at cantonal level.
Voting rights for foreigners at municipal level also exist, for example, in the cantons of Vaud, Fribourg and Geneva.
Usually you must already have lived in Switzerland or the canton for several years.
Some German-speaking cantons allow their municipalities to introduce it themselves.
The topic is often discussed and voted on politically.

abschnitte.titel: What are voting rights for foreigners?
abschnitte.text: **Voting rights for foreigners** allow people without a Swiss passport to take part in votes and sometimes also in elections. In Switzerland about a quarter of the population does not have a Swiss passport. Many of them have lived here for a long time, work and pay taxes. Whether they may have a say is decided by the **cantons** themselves.

Only Swiss citizens may take part in national votes and elections. For cantons and municipalities, however, the rules of the **cantonal constitution** apply. There a canton can introduce voting rights for foreigners. Sometimes they may only vote, sometimes they may also take part in elections or even be elected themselves.

It goes furthest in the cantons of **Jura** and **Neuchâtel**, where foreigners may also vote at cantonal level. Neuchâtel has had voting rights for foreigners in its municipalities since the 19th century. In the cantons of Vaud, Fribourg and Geneva, too, foreigners may have a say in their municipality. In Appenzell Ausserrhoden, the Grisons and Basel-Stadt the municipalities may decide for themselves, and a few have introduced it.

Anyone who wants to vote usually needs a **settlement permit** or must have lived in Switzerland for a certain number of years. Depending on the canton this is, for example, five or ten years. You must also be of age, that is 18 years old. The exact rules are slightly different in each canton.

**Supporters** say that anyone who has lived here for a long time and pays taxes should also have a say. **Opponents** think that anyone who wants to have a say should become naturalised. In many German-speaking cantons, voting rights for foreigners have been rejected in votes. The topic shows how differently the regions of Switzerland think about politics.

begriffe.erklaerung: The right to take part in votes.
The process by which a foreign person receives a Swiss passport.
Permission for foreigners to live in Switzerland permanently.
The most important law of a canton.

gewusst: The canton of Jura gave foreigners voting rights at cantonal level as soon as it was founded in 1979.
In some municipalities in French-speaking Switzerland, foreigners can even be elected to the municipal council.
Countries such as Sweden or New Zealand also have voting rights for foreigners.

teile.einleitung: The World Bank is an international organisation that supports poorer countries with development projects. It lends money for schools, roads, hospitals or water pipes and advises governments. Its big goal is to end extreme poverty in the world.
wichtigste: The World Bank supports poorer countries with development projects.
It was founded in 1944 at the Bretton Woods conference in the USA.
Its headquarters are in Washington, D.C.
It gives loans and grants to states, not to private individuals.
Almost all the countries in the world are members, Switzerland since 1992.
The World Bank is a specialised agency of the United Nations.
A sister organisation is the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

abschnitte.text: Despite its name, the **World Bank** is not a bank where you can open an account. Its customers are states, above all countries with low or middle incomes. It lends them money on favourable terms so that they can build important projects. The poorest countries often receive interest-free loans or grants that they do not have to pay back.

In July 1944, while the Second World War was still going on, representatives of 44 states met in **Bretton Woods** in the US state of New Hampshire.
